01 / 13 · Welcome

My name is Tina.

I know what it means to be shattered by shame, silenced by grief, and held together by performance.

I have walked through betrayal, infertility, burnout, and the kind of spiritual numbness that makes you wonder if God still sees you.

I kept going. I stayed faithful. I held it together on the outside while quietly falling apart on the inside.

Then I wrote a book, Five Good Years. Not to inspire anyone or build a platform. I wrote it because I needed to make sense of what had happened to me. Somewhere in telling the truth about my own story, something cracked open. My pain found purpose.

What started as a journal became a book.

What started as a cry became a calling.

What started as survival became a system.

We were each created with an original design. God placed a purpose, an identity and a calling in us before life ever had a chance to interfere. Loss, grief and shame can try to interrupt that design. It was disrupted. It was not destroyed.

They say grief has five stages. The last one is acceptance.

I got to a sixth. Redemption.

I did not build this to impress anyone. I built it because I had to survive, and then I realised I was not the only one.

I spent 20 years in corporate building products. Now I build people.

My purpose is to help women like you redeem the times and be restored to your original design, as we create beautiful stories from broken lives.

From broken to beautiful.

02 / 13 · You may be carrying

From the outside, you are still functioning.

But underneath, something feels fragile and unresolved.

01

You may be carrying...

Heartbreak. Grief. Disappointment. Infertility. Divorce. Or a quiet erosion of identity that you have not fully put words to yet.

02

You have tried...

Prayer. Staying busy. Staying positive. Listening to advice. Pushing yourself to keep going. And the weight is still there.

03

You are asking...

Can I trust myself again? Can I love again? What if time is running out? What if I choose wrong again?

04

You know...

Something has not been dealt with at the root. You are not just confused. You are carrying something that needs to be faced, processed, and rebuilt properly.

You are not behind. You are carrying something that needs proper attention.

You are celebrating other people's milestones while quietly grieving your own. You are tired of holding it together. And deep down, you know surface approaches have not been enough.

Why you are still stuck

It is not you. It is what you have been given to work with.

You have the faith and the tools, and you are putting in the effort. The gap is not you. None of these things was designed to do what you actually need right now.

Therapy

Valuable. Helps you understand patterns and process the past. But not designed to give you a structured, faith-rooted way to rebuild your life and sense of self when everything has been disrupted.

Prayer

Powerful. Connects you to God and gives you hope. But not designed to give you the sequence, accountability, and honest one to one support needed to actually rebuild.

Church

A gift. But hard to be truly honest in those circles. Most programs are underfunded. Tailored, long term, personal support is rarely available. And some women fear becoming the illustration in next Sunday's sermon.

As powerful as a hammer is, it is not used for surgery.

These are the right tools for what they were designed to do. What you need now requires something built specifically for this moment and this kind of rebuilding.

03 / 13 · The deeper truth

We have been chasing the wrong destination.

The story we were given: get married, have children, hit the milestones, then you will feel complete. But look at what actually happens across all three groups of women.

Three stories. The same feeling underneath.

Women who have everything.

The marriage. The children. The home. The life that looks exactly like the plan. And they are still empty. Still searching. Still wondering why.

Women who have some of it.

A marriage but no children. Children but no marriage. The career but not the relationship. The emptiness is still there, sitting alongside what they did build.

Women who have none of it.

The divorce came. The miscarriage. The hysterectomy. The relationship that ended. The timeline that did not hold. The emptiness is there too.

If the same emptiness shows up whether a woman has everything, something, or nothing, then we can agree that the destination was never the thing.

Marriage, motherhood and milestones are a proxy.

What every woman really wants is identity, wholeness, purpose, and to know her life counts.

This is what I help women build. Together, we build you into a woman who is whole in herself and rooted in God's truth about who she is, not in the world's verdict or expectations of her or her accomplishments.

06 / 13 · Your 90 days

01

Reveal

From there, you identify what is really going on beneath the surface. You name the root wound and what has not been fully processed.

09 / 13 · Who this is for

Is this the right next step for you?

This work is for a woman who is ready to do it properly. Here is how to know.

This is for you if

You are ready to rebuild.

  • You are a Christian woman in a corporate career who knows life has not gone according to plan and is ready to do the inner work to rebuild with peace, confidence and intention.
  • You are still functioning, but you know something deeper needs attention. Prayer, endurance and staying busy have not reached the root.
  • You may be carrying heartbreak, disappointment, infertility, divorce or timeline grief.
  • You are open to honest reflection, personal responsibility and real change. You need more than encouragement.

This is not for you if

You want it done for you.

  • You want a quick fix, surface-level motivation, or someone to rescue you while you remain passive.
  • You are unwilling to reflect honestly or take responsibility.
  • You need clinical or therapeutic support right now.

11 / 13 · Why this matters now

What it costs to keep carrying it.

You are good at functioning. But unresolved pain does not stay where you left it. It follows you into your relationships, your decisions and your everyday life.

Many women say they want to break generational patterns.

Then, without meaning to, they build new ones and tie them with a beautiful bow. It looks like a different life. Underneath, it is the same cycle.

You were handed a boilerplate life.

A template for how a woman’s life should go. Nobody gave you room to question it. So you may never have asked yourself what you truly want, and answered honestly.

When your life does not fit the mould, you begin to shrink.

The comparison starts. Your confidence slips. You hide, or you settle for less because you think it is the best you can have.

You were never meant to hold your head lower. You are meant to stand as the queen you are.

The graveyard is full of unused gifts.

Talents never tapped. Ideas never started. Palliative care nurse Bronnie Ware found that the regret she heard most from people near the end of life was not having had the courage to live a life true to themselves, instead of the one others expected of them.

I live by one belief: live full, die empty.

I never thought I would be happy again.

I never thought I could build a life worth living. When you cannot see the next step, everything goes dark.

What changed it for me was a new perspective, and the courage to step out in faith and begin again. Sometimes that courage comes from one person who has walked the path and can show you there is another way.

You do not have to see the whole path. You only need someone who has walked it to show you the next step.

There is no deadline here. There is only the next decision you will make, and who you will be when you make it.

13 / 13 · Questions

Questions you may be asking.

Short, honest answers. For anything else, ask on your clarity call.

Who is this for, and who is it not for?

It is for Christian women in corporate careers whose lives look successful from the outside but have not gone the way they planned, and who are ready to do the honest inner work of rebuilding. If you want a quick fix, or someone to carry it for you, this may not be your season.

Do I need to be a Christian?

Not at all. My work is rooted in faith and Christian principles, and that shapes our conversations. If you are comfortable with that, you are so welcome here.

Is this therapy?

No. This is coaching, not therapy. Together we look at your story, your decisions and what comes next. If you need more than coaching can give, please seek support from the right professional, whether that is a therapist, a counsellor or your healthcare provider. There is no shame in that.

How does it work?

Ninety days, one to one. We begin with a private kickoff call. Then we have a live call at the start and close of each phase, Reveal, Restore and Rebuild, with Margin Notes to hold you in between.

What is the 30 day bonus?

If you have done all of the work and still have not reached the objectives we agreed, I walk with you for 30 more days at no extra cost, by voice and video note, so you get to where you need to be.

Can I reach you between sessions?

Yes, through Margin Notes. Write or record whenever something comes up and I reply within 48 hours, Monday to Thursday, with a voice or video note. You are not left to figure it out alone.

What happens on the clarity call?

It is a 30 minute, no pressure conversation. You tell me what you are carrying, and we look honestly at whether this is the right next step. You leave with one thing you can do this week. If it is not the right fit, I will tell you.

How many women do you work with?

A small number at a time. This work needs my full presence and personal attention, so I keep it limited on purpose.

How does payment work?

The investment is £3,200 when you pay in full. Payment plans are available, and we talk through the options on your clarity call.
